completion_promises.criterion_text: await adapter.start() connects to NATS, registers the manifest in agent-registry, subscribes to the command subject, starts the heartbeat loop, and sets _ready — verified via mocked NATSClient in unit tests.
completion_promises.evidence: NATSAdapter.start() calls client.connect() (line 142), client.register_agent(manifest) (line 152) which publishes to fleet.register and writes the agent-registry KV bucket, client.subscribe_with_reply on Topics.resolve(Topics.Agents.COMMAND, agent_id=...) (line 170), creates the named heartbeat task (line 180), then sets self._ready (line 188). All five steps are pinned by TestStartLifecycle (5 tests: connects, registers manifest, subscribes, begins heartbeat loop, sets ready event).

completion_promises.criterion_text: Subscription uses subscribe_with_reply, not subscribe (Bug #1 regression guard — assert via mock call inspection).
completion_promises.evidence: NATSAdapter.start() calls self._client.subscribe_with_reply(command_subject, self._on_command) (line 170). TestSubscribeWithReplyContract has three explicit guard tests: test_start_uses_subscribe_with_reply asserts subscribe_with_reply was awaited; test_start_does_not_use_plain_subscribe asserts subscribe was NEVER awaited; test_subscription_callback_is_adapter_wrapper verifies the callback is the adapter's _on_command (so reply_to flows through to the router). The implementation also includes an inline comment block referencing Bug #1.

completion_promises.criterion_text: await adapter.stop() deregisters, cancels heartbeat, drains in-flight (within 30s shutdown_timeout), and closes the connection.
completion_promises.evidence: NATSAdapter.stop() unsubscribes (line 224), drains in-flight commands using a deadline + 0.05s poll up to self._shutdown_timeout=30.0s (lines 234-247), cancels self._heartbeat_task and awaits its CancelledError (lines 252-258), publishes deregistration via client.deregister_agent(agent_id, reason='shutdown') (lines 263-273), disconnects (lines 275-282), and clears _ready (line 286). TestStopLifecycle covers all these paths in 8 tests including drain success, drain timeout, deregister failure recovery, and the 30.0s default shutdown_timeout.

completion_promises.criterion_text: Heartbeat publishes at the configured interval (test with a stub clock or short interval).
completion_promises.evidence: NATSAdapter._heartbeat_loop reads self._config.heartbeat_interval_seconds (line 312), publishes AgentHeartbeatPayload via client.heartbeat(payload), then sleeps for the interval, looping until cancelled. TestHeartbeatLoop has 6 tests using a sub-second interval (0.01s) post-construction override: publishes_at_least_once, publishes_multiple_times (≥3 fires in 100ms), payload_carries_agent_id, status_ready_when_idle, status_busy_when_active, and loop_survives_publish_error.

completion_promises.criterion_text: Active-task counter increments on on_command start and decrements on completion (so stop() knows when to wait).
completion_promises.evidence: NATSAdapter._on_command wraps the router invocation in a try/finally that increments self._active_tasks before delegating to self._command_router.on_command and decrements in the finally branch (lines 295-302). TestActiveTaskCounter has 4 tests: starts_at_zero, increments_then_decrements (asserts counter==1 mid-call via an observing handler), decrements_even_on_router_exception (proves exception-safety), and forwards_envelope_and_reply_to (proves transparent delegation).

completion_promises.criterion_text: Integration test (against a real NATS via nats-server in test fixture or testcontainers): full start → dispatch one command → stop round-trip succeeds, with the manifest visible in agent-registry between start and stop.
completion_promises.evidence: Integration test against real nats-server is OUT OF SCOPE for this turn due to the file-count constraint at minimal documentation level (max 2 files: source + test). The task does not declare requires_infrastructure, no nats-server is running locally, and creating a third test file would violate the autobuild protocol. The unit-test surface exhaustively covers the lifecycle seam with a mocked NATSClient (30 tests covering start/stop ordering, subscribe_with_reply contract, heartbeat periodicity, active-task counter, and topic resolution), and the underlying NATSClient.register_agent / deregister_agent / heartbeat / subscribe_with_reply primitives have their own integration coverage in nats-core. A follow-up task can add tests/integration/test_adapter_lifecycle.py with a docker-compose nats-server fixture.
